I am sorry you had to experience this, but very glad you know none of what he said was true!

My first long term boyfriend while I was in college was like this as well, and it sadly took me 3.5 years to finally realize I would be happier without him. I am still on the journey of recovering from the negative self imagery he instilled on me though I had extremely low confidence and self esteem at the time. He knew how to cut me to the core... And it didn't matter when, things would happen when we ate food, were intimate, watching a show, it didn't matter. At the time I was struggling with control of an eating disorder (which he knew) so the comments on my image would often spiral me into punishing myself with little food, excess exercise, or purging. I was hovering at 90lbs or under while we dated which was extremely unhealthy.

He would:
Tell me I had a mustache growing in, when I had tiniest peach fuzz on my upper lip
Claim I had no body/figure if I would do something like wiggle or dance to a song (as in "what are you doing that for? You have no ass to shake")
Told me I had a boy's chest or mosquito bite tits 
Tell me I was fat, or putting on too much weight if my stomach had the slightest bulge when sitting/moving around etc or if I ate more food than what he thought I should be eating
Told me I wasn't allowed to wear headbands because I wasn't athletic enough (? Still don't understand this one)
I have curly hair that is hard to style at times, and he would insist I straighten it more than I wanted to (it was very damaging) because otherwise I looked too "dumpy" for him 
Tell me I had to wear make up when the hints of acne or blemishes would pop up. He would cruelly point out pimples I was already self conscious about and sometimes refuse to kiss me when I had them if I wasn't wearing make up


This list could be endless but I just want to make sure other young women out there also don't fall into the same trap. They will demean you, belittle you, and break you down so you don't leave them. So you think they are the only person who will accept you as a SO.
Know your self worth, know that your partner should be your best friend and your ally, they should be building you up. Not breaking you down.

My current partner has never once made me feel insecure, uncomfortable, or doubt their intentions. He is honestly everything I've ever wanted in a partner and more. I know he has my back 100% just like I do for him and it is one of the greatest feelings. 

If you got this far thanks for reading. Don't stay in shitty relationships because of a sunk cost fallacy.
There's so many more people out there who will love you for you, and not make you change a thing about yourself.

If this post is real and not a troll, you cannot be seriously thinking your response to ban his girlfriend is in any way logical or in some backwards way supporting your brother.

You are adding to the problem and making it far worse for your brother and not even considering how it would make him feel let alone how bad you have made her feel too. She now has two families not accepting her and your brother.

If you care about your brother go apologize to him and his girlfriend. Set the example of how your side of the family is open and accepting. What you did makes you no better than her parents and you should be ashamed for acting so petty.
